newsitem.title: USA: Destron Fearing microchip okayed by USDA.
newsitem.headline: Destron Fearing microchip okayed by USDA.

text.p: Destron Fearing Corp said Monday the U.S. Department of Agriculture has given clearance for the implanting of microchips in food animals.
Destron said the approval clears the way for the company to market its electronic identification products to the livestock industry.
Implantation of Destron EID devices was previously cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, subject to USDA concurrence as to anatomical implant sites in an animal.

Destron said the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service has identified four implantation sites, all in inedible tissue, where it has been demonstrated there will be minimal or no migration of the implanted device.

"This is another significant milestone as we work to create a market for implantable identification in the livestock industry," Randolph Geissler, president and chief executive of Destron Fearing, said in a statement. "This will enable us to begin actively promoting our implantable system to the livestock industry, and we anticipate that it will also result in the increased use of microchips in control programs for diseases such as equine infectious anemia."
